hypothesis: The front-end has no held fetch-request state: imem_valid/imem_addr are re-driven from the (advancing) PC every cycle and imem_ready is not used to freeze the request. When the teacher memory model injects a wait state (imem_ready=0), the address changes underneath the outstanding request, triggering the repeated 'I-memory request changed before ready' checks. Each of these aborted fetches drops or duplicates an instruction word, so the executed program diverges from the fetched stream — this is why the ooo_load_overlap test retires with wrong architectural state (x16=0x0f vs 0x73, x18=0x11 vs 0x75) and its store to DMEM[0x304] never lands (stays 0xa5a5a5a5). On a long benchmark such as bench_crc32_64bytes the same instruction corruption prevents the stream from ever reaching the ECALL, so halted never asserts and the run blows the 20 s simulation budget — the single reported failure. The mechanism is a missing registered, stable fetch request (assert imem_valid=1, keep imem_addr/PC frozen until the imem_ready beat, then capture imem_rdata and advance) plus top-level gating that must stall PC/IF-FD while a fetch is outstanding and must not let the predictive next-PC move imem_addr before ready. This is distinct from the earlier 'stall-everything' / 'dmem-only hold' framings: the fix is a proper fetch handshake FSM whose request register is decoupled from the live PC, not a blanket pipeline freeze.
constraints: Top-level port list and names of rv32i5 are frozen; do not rename/remove any output port (imem_*, dmem_*, dbg_*, halted, exit_code, dbg_features).
While imem_valid=1 and imem_ready=0: imem_valid must stay 1 and imem_addr must remain bit-identical until imem_ready is sampled high; imem_addr[1:0] must always be 00.
Capture imem_rdata only on the ready beat, then advance PC; do not consume/re-fetch the same word on a wait cycle.
Branch-predictor redirect must not change imem_addr while a fetch is still awaiting ready (hold or defer redirection).
dmem transactions (SW/SH/SB be encoding: SW=1111, SH=addr[1]?1100:0011, SB=0001<<addr[1:0]) must similarly hold dmem_valid/we/addr/wdata/be stable until dmem_ready, then complete the store.
Only wb_stage may assert halted/exit_code, and only for a committed ECALL 0x00000073; reset semantics: synchronous active-low rst_n, dmem_valid=0 during reset.
Do not change teacher TB, spec, or any file outside the allowed RTL list; no hardcoded test vectors or faked debug/feature flags.
Respect Icarus -g2012 limits: no variable part-selects, no constant-index array writes inside always_*, no break/continue, no whole-array assignment.
verification_targets: 'I-memory request changed before ready' check must produce 0 occurrences (currently ~17 in ooo_load_overlap_rename).
ooo_load_overlap_rename: x16 must equal 0x00000073 (currently 0x0f), x18 must equal 0x00000075 (currently 0x11).
ooo_load_overlap_rename: DMEM[0x00000304] must become 0x00000075 (currently 0xa5a5a5a5) — store completes.
simulation_timeout must clear: bench_crc32_64bytes (and all tests) must reach halted=1 with the expected exit_code well within the cycle/time budget, instead of the run being cut at 20 s.
imem_addr[1:0] must be 00 on every cycle and imem_addr stable across any imem_ready=0 window.
rejected_hypotheses: Attempt 5 (blanket fetch gating causing deadlock at imem_addr=0x0c) — the pipeline now advances and halts the ooo test, so a full freeze is wrong; the defect is request stability/capture, not a permanent stall.

Attempt 6 (dmem-only request-hold fix) — 'I-memory request changed before ready' still dominates and the store to DMEM[0x304] still fails, so the imem side and fetch-instruction integrity are still broken.

Attempts 1-3 (capability bit / port binding / BP-update plumbing) — elaboration succeeds and predictors/resolution are no longer the first-observed failing checks; the current blocker is memory handshake protocol, not capability declaration

Assumption that the teacher memory model is strictly single-cycle zero-wait — the observed ready=0 wait states and corresponding protocol checks show the fetch path must honor a real valid/ready handshake.
